view_frame: The drawing provides a single TOP (XY) view. The world coordinate system is defined as: X is width (horizontal in view), Y is depth (vertical in view), and Z is height/thickness (perpendicular to the view). The origin (0,0,0) is assumed at the bottom-left corner of the block's footprint on the bottom face (Z=0). The block extends from X=0 to 40, Y=0 to 30, and Z=0 to 12.

features.axis_or_plane: XY plane footprint, extruded along Z
features.evidence: Text 'Body: 40 wide x 30 deep x 12 thick' and the rectangular outline in the TOP view with dimensions 40 and 30.

features.placement: Centre axis at (X=20, Y=15). Extents: Z[0, 12] (through-hole).
features.evidence: Circle in the TOP view labelled 'Ø8'. Text 'Opening centred in top face'. Clarification answer confirms 'through'.

connections: The opening_centre is a subtractive feature from the block_body.
The opening_centre axis is coincident with the geometric centre of the block_body in the XY plane.
edit_rules: If block_body width (X) changes, the opening_centre X coordinate must update to width/2 to maintain centring.
If block_body depth (Y) changes, the opening_centre Y coordinate must update to depth/2 to maintain centring.
If block_body thickness (Z) changes, the opening_centre Z extents must update to [0, new_thickness] to maintain the through-hole status.
If opening_centre diameter changes, the circle radius in the top view updates, but the centre coordinates remain fixed relative to the block centre.
